facts.statement: Braunosteus fossils date to the Late Frasnian stage.
The genus Braunosteus was named by Stensiö in 1959.
Braunosteus schmidti is a medium-sized arthrodire placoderm found in the Late Devonian Kellwasserkalk facies of Bad Wildungen, Germany.
facts.quote: Braunosteus schmidti is a medium-sized selenosteid arthrodire placoderm known from the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Late Devonian Bad Wildungen, Germany.

facts.statement: B. schmidti had a broad skull approximately 9 centimeters long with a short, pointed snout.
facts.quote: B. schmidti has a broad skull about 9 centimeters long, and a short, but pointed rostrum.

facts.statement: The appearance of Braunosteus is very similar to the basal selenosteid Pachyosteus.
facts.quote: Its appearance is very similar to that of the basal selenosteid Pachyosteus.

facts.statement: Erik Stensiö originally classified Braunosteus in the monotypic family Braunosteidae in 1959.
facts.quote: It was originally placed within a monotypic family, "Braunosteidae," by Erik Stensiö in 1959.

facts.statement: Obruchev and Miles later placed the genus in the family Trematosteidae because of a postpineal fenestra.
facts.quote: Obruchev (1964) and Miles (1969) placed it within the Trematosteidae due to the presence of a postpineal fenestra.

facts.statement: Denison placed B. schmidti in Selenosteidae in 1978, citing shared postpineal fenestrae, orbital anatomy, and scapulo-coracoid bone similarity with Pachyosteus and Enseosteus.
facts.quote: Denison (1978) has B. schmidti placed within Selenosteidae, noting that other arthrodires in addition to trematosteids have postpineal fenestrae, as well as similar anatomy of the orbital and suborbital plates, and that its scapulo-coracoid bone is largely identical to those of Pachyosteus and Enseosteus.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Braunosteus as Braunosteidae.
Braunosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
